EX-001.text: A moth ate words. When I heard of that wonder, it seemed to me a strange thing—that the worm should swallow the riddle of certain men, a thief in the darkness, and their glorious pronouncements.
EX-001.clue: This creature loves knowledge more than you do—it consumes words.
EX-001.source: [Anglo-Saxon Riddles of the Exeter Book/Annotated/42 - Wikisource](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Anglo-Saxon_Riddles_of_the_Exeter_Book/Annotated/42); [The riddles of the Exeter book - Internet Archive](https://archive.org/stream/riddlesofexeterbook00tuppuoft/riddlesofexeterbook00tuppuoft_djvu.txt)
EX-001.licence: Public domain; translation by Paull Franklin Baum (1963)

EX-002.text: I am a most strange creature, for I satisfy women, a single thing by nature. No harm do I inflict on the creatures of this estate if the man who inhabits the stronghold wishes to use me rightly.
EX-002.clue: You use me to grant access to what is kept hidden.
EX-002.licence: Public domain; Exeter Book (original manuscript c. 10th century)

EX-003.text: I stand with my feet in the earth, a warrior with twisted limbs. I am strong, I wage fierce war.
EX-003.clue: I break ground to feed the people.

EX-004.text: I am silent when I walk, when I eat, when I drink; but when I sleep I roar fearfully.
EX-004.clue: A loyal companion that barks in dreams.
EX-004.source: [Anglo-Saxon Riddles of the Exeter Book/Index of Solutions - Wikisource](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Anglo-Saxon_Riddles_of_the_Exeter_Book/Index_of_Solutions)

EX-005.text: Boneless it dwells in bosom, boneless flows out; hard in head, soft in breast, it gives glory to noble kinsmen and comfort to the common folk.
EX-005.clue: I consume but leave ash; I warm but can burn.

EX-006.text: I am a precious thing, wrapped in skin, adorned with hair. I am the delight of warriors, ornament of nobles.
EX-006.clue: I hang at a warrior's side, both decoration and death-dealer.

EX-007.text: I travel over the mountains and through vales, through groves and along glens. I am carried in hand and brought to hall; I lodge in the breast.
EX-007.clue: I sail the seas but also dwell in hearts.

EX-008.text: I am bound yet have no chains. I move the whole year yet never grow weary. Bright is my home, and I am a creature that dreads evil men.
EX-008.clue: I can be solid or liquid, and all life depends on me.

GR-001.text: What creature goes on four feet in the morning, two feet at noon, and three feet in the evening?
GR-001.clue: This being changes its form throughout a lifetime.
GR-001.tradition: The Riddle of the Sphinx (Greek mythology), posed to Oedipus
GR-001.source: [Riddle of the Sphinx - Quatr.us Study Guides](https://quatr.us/greeks/riddle-sphinx-oedipus.htm); [The Sphinx – Mythology Unbound](https://uen.pressbooks.pub/mythologyunbound/chapter/sphinx/)

NO-001.text: What is the name of the horse that draws the chariot of day across the sky?
NO-001.clue: His mane illuminates the night sky.
NO-001.tradition: Norse Mythology, Vafthrudnismal (wisdom contest of Odin and Vafthrudnir)
NO-001.source: [The Poetic Edda: Vafthruthnismol - Internet Sacred Text Archive](https://sacred-texts.com/neu/poe/poe05.htm)

NO-002.text: What is the name of the horse that the giant Hrym rode when the bonds are broken?
NO-002.clue: A steed that rides at the end of all things.
NO-002.source: [The Poetic Edda: Vafthruthnismol - Internet Sacred Text Archive](https://sacred-texts.com/neu/poe/poe05.htm)

EN-001.text: Little Nancy Etticote, in a white petticoat, with a red nose; the longer she stands, the shorter she grows.
EN-001.clue: I burn away as I illuminate.

EN-002.text: In marble halls as white as milk, lined with a skin as soft as silk; within a fountain crystal-clear, a golden apple doth appear. No doors there are to this stronghold, yet thieves break in and steal the gold.
EN-002.clue: Layers of protection hide the treasure inside.
EN-002.source: [In Marble Walls As White As Milk - Mama Lisa's World](https://www.mamalisa.com/?t=es&p=1729)
EN-002.licence: Public domain (collected in Leslie Brooke's 1916 nursery rhyme collection)

EN-003.text: Two legs sat upon three legs, with one leg in his lap; in comes four legs, and runs away with one leg. Up jumps two legs, catches up three legs, throws it after four legs, and makes him bring one leg back.
EN-003.canonicalAnswer: A man sitting on a stool with a leg of mutton; a dog steals it
EN-003.displayAnswer: A man sitting on a stool with a leg of mutton; a dog steals it
EN-003.clue: A feast interrupted by a thief with four paws.

EN-004.text: I have a little sister; they call her Peep, Peep. She wades the water, deep, deep, deep; she climbs the mountains, high, high, high. Poor little thing! she has but one eye.
EN-004.displayAnswer: A bird's eye (or potato eye, or spring of water)
EN-004.clue: It sees the world but cannot look both ways.

EN-005.text: Old Mother Twitchett had one eye, and a long tail which she let fly, and every time she went over a gap, she left a bit of her tail in a trap.
EN-005.clue: I pierce cloth and leave my trace behind.

EN-006.text: Peter White will ne'er go right; would you know the reason why? He follows his nose wherever he goes, and that stands all awry.
EN-006.clue: A crooked helper that serves by following its bent nature.

EN-007.text: As white as milk, as black as coal, as soft as silk, with a heart of gold.
EN-007.clue: A simple treasure found in nature, white and dark together.

JW-001.text: Out of the eater came something to eat, and out of the strong came something sweet.
JW-001.clue: A bee's home grew inside a predator.

JW-002.text: Seven issue and nine enter; two yield draught, one drinks.
JW-002.canonicalAnswer: Seven days of menstruation; nine months of pregnancy; two breasts; one child
JW-002.displayAnswer: Seven days of menstruation; nine months of pregnancy; two breasts; one child
JW-002.source: [The Riddles of Solomon in Rabbinic Literature - Wikisource](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Folk-Lore/Volume_1/The_Riddles_of_Solomon_in_Rabbinic_Literature)

JW-003.clue: A fortress of flesh that contains new life.
JW-003.source: [The Riddles of Solomon in Rabbinic Literature - Wikisource](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Folk-Lore/Volume_1/The_Riddles_of_Solomon_in_Rabbinic_Literature)

JW-004.text: Living moves not; head cut off, moves.
JW-004.clue: Once alive as a tree, now silent wood that travels.
JW-004.source: [The Riddles of Solomon in Rabbinic Literature - Wikisource](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Folk-Lore/Volume_1/The_Riddles_of_Solomon_in_Rabbinic_Literature)

JW-005.text: Dead lived, grave moves, dead prays.
JW-005.clue: A man swallowed by the sea yet called upon his God.
JW-005.tradition: Solomon's Riddle from Rabbinic Literature (biblical allusion)
JW-005.source: [The Riddles of Solomon in Rabbinic Literature - Wikisource](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Folk-Lore/Volume_1/The_Riddles_of_Solomon_in_Rabbinic_Literature)

CH-001.text: This lovely maiden eats no meat but eats leaves. She labours each day spinning and weaving for the benefit of others.
CH-001.clue: A humble spinner that works itself to death for silk.
CH-001.source: [8 Lantern Riddles to Celebrate the Chinese Lantern Festival - The Epoch Times](https://www.theepochtimes.com/8-lantern-riddles-to-celebrate-the-chinese-lantern-festival_1271134.html)

CH-002.text: He devotes his life to looking after the house. His mate always follows when the master goes out.
CH-002.source: [8 Lantern Riddles to Celebrate the Chinese Lantern Festival - The Epoch Times](https://www.theepochtimes.com/8-lantern-riddles-to-celebrate-the-chinese-lantern-festival_1271134.html)

CH-003.text: It's been around for millions of years, but it's no more than a month old.
CH-003.clue: Ancient in the sky, forever renewing itself.
CH-003.source: [8 Lantern Riddles to Celebrate the Chinese Lantern Festival - The Epoch Times](https://www.theepochtimes.com/8-lantern-riddles-to-celebrate-the-chinese-lantern-festival_1271134.html)

CH-004.text: What belongs to you but others use it more than you do?
CH-004.clue: Others speak it more often than you hear it.
CH-004.source: [8 Lantern Riddles to Celebrate the Chinese Lantern Festival - The Epoch Times](https://www.theepochtimes.com/8-lantern-riddles-to-celebrate-the-chinese-lantern-festival_1271134.html)

CH-005.text: It works hard all its life, counting numbers day and night, but never gets past 12.
CH-005.clue: It measures time by numbers that repeat.
CH-005.source: [8 Lantern Riddles to Celebrate the Chinese Lantern Festival - The Epoch Times](https://www.theepochtimes.com/8-lantern-riddles-to-celebrate-the-chinese-lantern-festival_1271134.html)

CH-006.text: They look like twin brothers, both sturdy and tall. They work together and go everywhere together.
CH-006.clue: A pair of helpers that deliver food to your mouth.
CH-006.source: [8 Lantern Riddles to Celebrate the Chinese Lantern Festival - The Epoch Times](https://www.theepochtimes.com/8-lantern-riddles-to-celebrate-the-chinese-lantern-festival_1271134.html)

CH-007.text: I can follow you for thousands of miles and not miss home. I do not fear cold or fire.
CH-007.clue: It leaves when the light does, but never truly leaves you.
CH-007.source: [8 Lantern Riddles to Celebrate the Chinese Lantern Festival - The Epoch Times](https://www.theepochtimes.com/8-lantern-riddles-to-celebrate-the-chinese-lantern-festival_1271134.html)

AF-001.text: My house has no doors or windows; yet there are living things within.
AF-001.clue: Break me open and find life waiting.

AF-002.text: I have a head and a tail but no body.
AF-002.clue: Two sides, no life, yet humans treasure me.
AF-002.licence: Public domain (traditional folklore, compiled by Laura Gibbs)

AF-003.text: What looks like a house but has many windows?
AF-003.displayAnswer: A fish trap (or honeycomb, or sieve)
AF-003.clue: It catches what swims or flows through it.

AF-004.text: I travel all around the world but never leave my corner.
AF-004.clue: I stick to messages and journey across continents.
AF-004.licence: Public domain (collected in modern African riddle traditions)

FO-001.text: The more you take, the more you leave behind. What am I?
FO-001.clue: I mark where you have been.
FO-001.tradition: Universal folk riddle (widespread in many traditions)

FO-002.text: Four hang, two point the way, two are useful, one sits in judgment, and the rest do the work.
FO-002.clue: A common farm animal whose parts serve many purposes.
FO-002.tradition: Universal folk riddle (widespread across Indo-European traditions)

FO-003.text: I have a face and two hands, but no arms and no legs.
FO-003.clue: I measure the passing of each day.

FO-004.text: I speak without a mouth and hear without ears. I have no body, but I come alive with wind. What am I?
FO-004.clue: I repeat your words but live in emptiness.

FO-005.text: I can travel around the world while staying in a corner.
FO-005.clue: Glued to paper, I go everywhere letters go.

FO-006.text: The rich need me. The poor have me. If you eat me, you will die. What am I?
FO-006.clue: The wealthy cannot afford to lack it; the poor have only this.

FO-007.text: What is seen in the middle of March and April that cannot be seen at any other time of year?
FO-007.clue: Look at the spelling of the months.

FO-008.text: What has a bed but never sleeps, has a bank but no money, and has a mouth but never speaks?

FO-009.text: What is harder to catch the faster you run?
FO-009.clue: The more you exert yourself, the more elusive it becomes.

FO-010.text: What can be cracked, made, told, and played?
FO-010.clue: It brings laughter when delivered well.

FO-011.text: What has a heart that does not beat?
FO-011.clue: A thorny plant with a tender center.

FO-012.text: What walks on four legs in the morning, two legs at noon, and three legs in the evening?
FO-012.displayAnswer: A human being (at different life stages; variant of Sphinx riddle)
FO-012.clue: This is life's journey measured in feet.
FO-012.tradition: Universal folk riddle (variant of Sphinx riddle)

FO-013.text: I am taken from a mine and shut up in a wooden case, from which I am never released. What am I?
FO-013.clue: I write the world but am imprisoned in wood.

FO-014.text: What comes once in a minute, twice in a moment, and never in one thousand years?

FO-015.text: What has roots that nobody sees, is taller than trees, up, up it goes, and yet it never grows?
FO-015.clue: Ancient stone that reaches the sky.

FO-016.text: What is black when you buy it, red when you use it, and gray when you throw it away?
FO-016.clue: I fuel fires but am destroyed by them.

FO-017.text: What question can you never answer "yes" to?
FO-017.clue: Answer it and you contradict yourself.

FO-018.text: What can fill a room but takes up no space?
FO-018.clue: It comes from sun, lamp, or fire.

FO-019.text: I am not alive, but I grow. I don't have lungs, but I need air. I don't have a mouth, but water kills me. What am I?
FO-019.clue: I am born of heat and feed on fuel.

FO-020.text: I speak all languages and have visited every country in the world. What am I?
FO-020.clue: I repeat what you say in any tongue.

FO-021.text: What is white and fluffy, and when you touch it, it rains?
FO-021.clue: I float in the sky and bring water to earth.

FO-022.text: I am always coming but never arrive. What am I?
FO-022.clue: It is always promised but never truly comes.

FO-023.text: What is the difference between a apple and an orange?
FO-023.canonicalAnswer: (This is a trick question; the answer is "I don't know" or depends on context)
FO-023.displayAnswer: (This is a trick question; the answer is "I don't know" or depends on context)
FO-023.clue: This may not have a single answer.

FO-024.text: I have a neck but no head. What am I?
FO-024.clue: I hold liquids but cannot drink them.

FO-025.text: What word becomes shorter when you add two letters to it?

FO-026.text: What is the one thing that all wise men, regardless of their politics or religion, agree is between heaven and earth?
FO-026.clue: It divides what we see above from what we see below.

FO-027.text: What is so fragile that saying its name breaks it?
FO-027.clue: It ends the moment you speak.
